# Simple Rules to Get Started

## **1\. Game Overview**

This is a tactical duel card game inspired by turn-based RPG combat.

Two players face off using squads of unique animal-based units with specialized classes and abilities. The game emphasizes fog of war, strategic movement, tactical attacks, and the smart use of items and terrain.

The Tacticlash battlefield is an analogy of the moment when enemy armies are already deployed and facing each other in the battlefield, so there’s no time for lengthy planning or complex unit positioning: quick thinking and fact-paced action are required each turn.

## **2\. Game objective**

Capture 15 of your opponent's units before they capture 15 of yours.

Players interested in express matches can set 10 captures as the goal.

## **3\. Game Components**

### Basic game

* 1 **Unit Deck** (32 unique characters)  
* 1 **Item Deck** (62 cards including gear, terrain, potions, and single-use effects)  
* **Coin** for coin-flip mechanics  
* 2 Battlefields (5x1 slots per player)  
* Damage markers (red) and status effects markers (orange)

### Advanced game (with Fortune Teller mechanics)

* 1 **Faction Deck** (12 faction cards, with 3 duplicates of each faction)  
* 1 **Tarot Deck** (13 unique Tarot cards)

## **4\. The Units Deck**

### Unit classes and class-specific buffs

| 🥊 Brawler (10 units, 31% of the deck) | ⚔️ Lancer (8 units – 25% of the deck) | 🎯 Shooter (8 units – 25% of the deck) | 🔮 Caster (6 units – 19% of the deck) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **» Strategic advantage:** Frontline enforcer — excels at holding positions and dealing steady pressure. | **» Strategic advantage:** Zonal controller — punishes enemy positioning and protects allies. | **» Strategic advantage:** Precision striker — best at picking off units from afar. | **» Strategic advantage:** Strategic disruptor — applies pressure and status from any position. |
| **» Range:** Attacks the tile directly in front. | **» Range:** Attacks diagonally forward (1 tile left/right). | **» Range:** Attacks any target 3+ tiles away. | **» Range:** Attacks any enemy unit on the board. |
| **» Class buff:** **Sturdy** — Starts with 2 HP. | **» Class buff:** **Counterattack** — Counters any attacks (even if not targeted) from within range. Flip a coin: on heads, block attack and hit back 1 HP. | **» Class buff: Longshot** — Extra damage if attacking from one edge of the board to the other (deals 2 HP damage instead of 1). | **» Class buff: Magic Paralysis** — Paralyzes surviving targets (they can't move nor attack next turn). |

### Rookies VS Veteran Units

* Some units are Rookies, some are Veterans.  
* Veteran units have veteran buffs, specific skills written in their cards.  
* Some of these buffs trigger when moving, attacking, being attacked, etc.  
* Keep an eye on your veteran unit’s buffs, even when they are not attacking or being attacked, since that might grant you strategic advantages.  
* See examples below:

| **Unit:** Korrin Windfeather (Gray Heron, Spear Master)**Class:** Lancer**Experience:** Rookie **Veteran buff:** N/A | **Unit:** Senya Longtail (Orange Cat, Witch)**Class:** Caster**Experience:** Veteran **Veteran buff:** “Hex Haze”: If this unit attacks this turn, next turn, if your opponent attacks, they flip a coin. If tails, negate the attack and inflict 1HP of damage to the attacker. You can’t use this skill next turn.  |
| Notes: Korrin is a rookie lancer unit, with no veteran buffs at his disposal. He can still use his class buff and counter attacks, though. | Notes: Senya is a veteran caster unit (fun fact: all caster units are veteran units\!) and can use her Hex Haze veteran buff to her advantage. She can also leverage her class buff on top of her veteran buff, unless otherwise specified for certain unit’s veteran buffs. |

## **5\. The Items Deck**

### Item types

**Gear — Armor (16 cards – 26%)**

* Equippable item that adds HP.  
* Light Armor fits squishy classes.  
* Heavy Armor fits Brawlers only.  
* If the unit equipped is face-down, so is their gear.

**Gear — Weapons & Accessories (10 cards – 16%)**

* Equippable item that adds unique effects.  
* Used to boost mobility, defense, or targeting.  
* Only 1 gear card per unit.  
* If the unit equipped is face-down, so is their gear.

**Single-Use Items (20 cards – 32%)**

* Instant effect, then discard.  
* Use for healing, disruption, or tactical tricks.  
* Does not count as gear.

**Terrain Cards (10 cards – 19%)**

* Placed face-up on any tile to affect the board.  
* Grants protection or disrupts movement/attacks.  
* Remains on the board until removed.

**Promotion Cards (4 cards – 7%)**

* Grants a unit with a class-specific upgrade.  
* Adds \+1 HP and unlocks a powerful new ability.  
* Counts as gear.

### Stacking gear

* Stacking is not allowed unless otherwise specified by a card effect: any given unit might have up to one piece of gear equipped at a time.  
* It is possible to swap equipped gear so new gear can be attached, keep in mind that the discarded gear immediately goes to the discard pile.  
* A unit that would be captured if their gear is removed (e.g. its HP will become 0\) cannot swap gear this way.

## **6\. Initial Setup**

1. Shuffle the **Unit Deck**.  
2. Each player draws **5 unit cards** from the unified deck.  
3. Each player places these 5 units **face-down**, in the order they desire, on any of their 5 available battlefield slots.  
4. Both rows of units face each other symmetrically in a 5x2 grid.  
5. Shuffle the **Item Deck** and make room for the discard pile.  
6. Start the game.

## **7\. Turn Structure**

### **A. Reinforcement Phase**

* At the start of your turn:  
* If any of your units were captured last turn and there are still unit cards in the deck, **draw 1 unit card** per captured unit and place it face-down (unless otherwise specified by card effects) in any open slot.  
* Draw **1 item card**.

### **B. Action Phase**

* Use items:  
  * Equip any gear as you wish.  
  * Place any terrain cards you wish.  
  * Use / Activate any single use items you wish.  
* Combat:  
  * Choose **1 unit** to act.  
  * You may **move** 1 slot left or right (swap with adjacent ally if needed). The moved unit is revealed, if face-down.  
  * You must then **attack**.  
  * **Attacking reveals** both the attacker and the target.

Review the detailed rules for a complete breakdown of **Combat rules**.

---

# Detailed Rules

## **1\. Fog of War**

* Units enter the board **face-down**, unless the contrary is specified by specific card effects.  
* Units are revealed when they **move**, **attack**, or **are attacked**.  
* Units remain face-down until revealed by game events.

## **2\. Movement**

* Units may move 1 tile left or right per turn, but only if they are selected for attacking that turn.  
* When moving, units must swap tiles with the units occupying the target tile.  
* Units carry gear when they move.  
* Terrain cards are not carried with movement.  
* Moved character is revealed (swapped allies are not).  
* **Regardless of movement, one unit must always attack each turn.**

## **3\. Combat**

* Players must clearly communicate which of their units they want to use for attacking each turn by:  
  * Revealing the attacking unit and equipped gear, if it’s face-down,  
  * announcing  and executing first any movement (optional),  
  * and immediately afterwards, the targeted enemy unit  
  * If the attacking unit’s attack will leverage any veteran buff or item card effect, it must be stated at this point  
* Before revealing the targeted unit, the opponent must declare if there is any effect preventing the attack, such as a veteran buff, terrain card effect, or a properly positioned lancer that will attempt to counter the attack. All of these possible events must be resolved before revealing the targeted unit, if the attack remains successful.  
* Then damage is calculated:  
  * Base damage is **1 point,** unless  
  * modified by class buffs, veteran buffs, and item effects  
* Lancers, Shooters and Casters have a **base HP of 1 point**, and Brawlers have a **base HP of 2 points**: HPs can be increased with the use of gear and certain card effects.  
* A unit is captured when their HP reaches 0  
* Place damage and/or effect markers on surviving units  
* If the attack results in losing any of the attacking party units (due for instance to counters or other effects), replace all captured units before passing to the next player’s turn.

## **4\. Endgame**

* If the Units deck is empty, defeated units are not replaced.  
* If a player has **no units** left on the board, they **lose**.  
* If a player cannot attack, they may move and pass.

---

# Advanced Rules: The Fortune Teller

## **1\. Initial Setup**

1. Shuffle the **Faction Deck** and the **Tarot Deck**.  
2. Reveal 4 random cards from the Tarot Deck, and place them in a row near the battlefield  
3. Place 4 random cards from the Faction Deck face down in a row, matching the positions of the 4 face-up Tarot cards

**2\. Revealing the fortune**

* Every time a player captures 5 units, reveal one of the face-down Faction cards (from left to right)  
* The effects of the Tarot card now apply to the revealed faction for the remainder of the game  
* Repeat when each player hits their 5 and 10 units captured marks  
* The effects of each Tarot card stacks, and remain valid until the end of the match  
* The same faction might be revealed more than once, and this is a valid outcome
